verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" (R1); "SPLASHDOWN! ... in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" (R2); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" (R4); "splash down off the coast of San Diego, California" (R5, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact location and successful splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown time ... scheduled for 5:07 p.m. PDT on April 10" (R1); "April 10, 2026" (R4, R5); "on Friday, April 10, 2026" (R5); "Friday, April 10" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state the date as April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down at 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and time zones match across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down approximately 50 to 100 miles offshore.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "about 50 to 80 miles offshore for the splashdown location" (R1); "more than 50 miles offshore" (R4); ship "50 to 100 miles off the coast" near splashdown (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources provide similar but not identical ranges (50-80 miles, >50 miles); claim's approximate range is supported but less precise.

verifications.claim: U.S. Navy recovery teams were stationed approximately 50 to 100 miles offshore for retrieval.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "50 to 100 miles off the coast in a westerly direction" for USS John P. Murtha (R8); "about 50 to 80 miles offshore" area (R1); "around 50 nautical miles off the coast of San Diego" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for Navy ship/recovery positioning at 50-100 miles offshore.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "approximate 10-day mission" (R2); "historic 10-day mission" (R4); "after 10 days" (R6); "10-day journey ... 10-day mission" (R7); "10-day mission" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as a 10-day mission across sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew was retrieved by the U.S. Navy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "U.S. Navy helicopters will then transport them to the ship"; "U.S. Navy extraction crew" (R2, R4); "U.S. Navy dive team assists" (R4); "Navy recovery ship" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit mentions of U.S. Navy involvement in crew extraction and transport.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew was transferred to Naval Air Station North Island.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The astronauts will be taken to Naval Air Station North Island, which is among the facilities that make up Naval Base Coronado."
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement in R8; aligned with general return to San Diego shore in other sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew included NASA's Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency's Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen" (R2); identical in R4, R6, R7
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names and affiliations match precisely.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew safely concluded the first crewed lunar mission since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first time since the Apollo missions ended in 1972" (R5); "first crewed mission into deep space in more than 50 years" (R6); "first humans in over 50 years to venture to the Moon" (R7); safe return confirmed throughout
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed lunar mission since 1972 (Apollo era) and safe conclusion.
